current_milestone: M1 — observables identified; offline system/preset-to-count inputs remain unresolved.
primary_objective: Predict the derelict's total searchable blue-box plus footlocker count offline from the smallest practical pre-traversal inputs. Treat the user's repeated matching counts as the working ground-truth assumption; do not request another physical count.
established_facts: User reports prior scene-index totals have always matched their observed derelict counts and instructs us to assume the total is correct. Treat as a user-authorized working assumption; no recount is required.

Count data currently span three CARGO_FLOATERS addresses with totals 51, 35, and 23; at address 00001A0004E84EFD, CARGO_FLOATERS=35 and MEDI_FLOATERS=16. Therefore preset is required; the dataset is still too small to prove a general system-input predictor.
Static scene-index calculation exactly reconstructs recorded per-room estimates from selected scene paths. Each searchable box is counted once as blue; footlockers remain separate.
The installed static DungeonOptions mapping has ten weighted presets, but the table has no direct crate-total field. Selected room-scene identities/multiplicities are needed to calculate the count.
The exact installed NMS.exe SHA-256 is 13d5060d4efb9d2a6a6b1b349bc4257231056cc2a055df4bb15d816262cc3499 (image base 0x140000000).

Hash-pinned existing analysis shows the dungeon-root resource path reads a descriptor seed and UseSeed flag before adding MODELS/SPACE/POI/DUNGEON.SCENE.MBIN; the producer of that descriptor and its relationship to crate-bearing room selection are not established.

New read-only .pdata disassembly of the root-event caller in the matching executable: RVA 02C0840E..02C089DA, size 1484; the call at 02C08607 is a virtual dispatch inside a generic queue/worker routine that manages and removes work nodes. It exposes no visible crate-count calculation, so this caller is not the count boundary.

Runner 0.1.21 has only fixed offline-check, offline-check-and-export, and crate-count-audit actions; it cannot accept a targeted RVA/function request. The audit only recomputes saved summary arithmetic.
The active gap is the deterministic mapping from pre-traversal inputs (likely system address plus preset and possibly a derived generation seed) to the selected room-scene multiset and its total.

A more targeted same-executable seed-lineage trace (agent/seed-lineage, commit 184ce2b30f0e674bd4a66429a9e73ddde80420c5; artifact blob 2b22a7bc7732efa0f95366b251d30b5cdb320e4d) shows RVA 006395D3 and 00639B99 both call helper 00639BE0; each helper return is passed as the owner argument to seed-consuming function 0063A6D0. The helper body and any write/forwarding of the seed fields remain unproven.
active_hypotheses: Selected room-scene identities and multiplicities determine the total through the static room index; the user's repeated physical matches authorize using that total without further tallying.
The room-variant selector may use the root descriptor seed and preset. The candidate producer path is shared helper 00639BE0; causation and smallest sufficient inputs remain unknown.
falsified_hypotheses: Root value alone determines total count, because the same saved address/root pair is associated with different totals under CARGO_FLOATERS and MEDI_FLOATERS.
Preset or room-family label alone gives a fixed total; selected room-scene variants have different indexed multiplicities.
The root-event caller at RVA 02C0840E is itself the crate-count producer.
Root value alone determines total; the same saved address/root with different presets has different totals.
latest_material_finding: The crate-count value is accepted as correct per the user's repeated matches. Existing same-build evidence narrows the next relevant seed path: two callers (RVA 006395D3 and 00639B99) share helper 00639BE0, whose return reaches the seed-consuming function at 0063A6D0. No available artifact shows whether 00639BE0 writes/forwards the seed. This is the next useful boundary to inspect.

latest_static_asset_experiment.question: Can the current static dungeon table alone encode total salvage/footlocker multiplicity, and has static scene composition drifted since the cached asset output?
latest_static_asset_experiment.finding: The table itself exposes no direct crate multiplicity, and a filename-index scan across installed PAKs found no other explicitly named freighter/dungeon table. Static target multiplicities vary by scene variant. The current index matches the cached 2026-10-09 common entries.
latest_static_asset_experiment.interpretation: Supports selected scene identity as necessary for indexed salvage/footlocker totals; no separately named freighter/dungeon table was found by the bounded filename filter. This does not establish the code-side selector, blue-crate composition, runtime selection, or physical total.

latest_static_crate_entity_experiment.question: Do room-scene CRATEM references correspond to an interactive salvage-crate entity, rather than only a generic decorative crate?
latest_static_crate_entity_experiment.finding: The selected CARG room MXML has three RefCrateM nodes targeting SPACEBASE/PROPS/CRATEM.SCENE.MBIN. The matching CRATEM entity defines GenericReward interaction, Id R_ABAND_CRATE, ScanName UI_SALVAGE_CRATE, and crate scanner icon. Separately, the DECORATION/CRATEM_PLACEMENT entity defines PartID _ABAND_CRATE_M; its placement scene is a locator.
latest_static_crate_entity_experiment.interpretation: Confirms these referenced CRATEM objects are configured salvage crates and supports the static scene index's salvage category. Does not prove every such prop spawns in the world, map it to the blue_crate F7 label, reveal runtime room selection, or predict total count.
